text:
tara: Quick design review — thinking about axis signposting + how we show extreme outliers on the CPU & latency charts. Posting mockups in a follow-up but want quick takes first.

sam: Agree this is a recurring pain. When a few spikes are 10x the norm the whole trend looks flat. Options: log scale, hard cap at p99/absolute value, or keep values but render spikes as a separate overlay. My preference: cap visually but surface the raw spikes via an overlay + tooltip. :thumbsup:

miguel: Accessibility note: if we visually cap, we need explicit axis annotation read by screen readers like "values capped at 2000 ms". Also ensure any overlay color passes contrast (WCAG 4.5) and that the spike overlay isn't the only cue — add pattern or dotted border for colorblind users.

zoe: Copy nit: legend items should be consistent: use "Median (P50)", "P90", "P99" rather than mixing words+percentiles. Also smoothing control should show the algorithm in the tooltip — e.g. "Smoothing: moving average, window=3". That helps engineers know what we're doing under the hood.

sam: Quick mock config I tried in the console (pseudo):
```
chart.type: time_series
series: [median, p90, p99]
axis.y.scale: linear
axis.y.cap: { mode: p99, value: 2000 } # visual cap only
overlay.spikes: { show: true, color: "#ff8c42", pattern: "diagonal-stripe", tooltip: "raw value: {val}ms" }
smoothing: { enabled: false, method: "ma", window: 3 }
```

tara: This is helpful. A few additional UX points: 1) When cap is active show a subtle chevron on the axis endpoint with hover that says "values above X are capped". 2) In the legend, include a tiny indicator for capped series like "median*" with a tooltip. 3) For user defaults, keep smoothing off but offer a quick toggle aggregated on the panel header.

miguel: +1 on chevron & screen reader announcement. For SR: add an aria-describedby pointing to a visually hidden paragraph: "Chart values above 2000 ms are visually capped; raw spikes available in overlay."

zoe: Regarding small screens: if the legend gets crowded, collapse to a single-line summary "Median (P50) • P90 • P99" and expand on tap. Also mobile should prefer overlay for spikes rather than tiny axis labels.

sam: Implementation note for infra: overlay will require exposing raw spike events from the timeseries ingestion layer so we can render exact raw values for tooltip. @miguel can you check with metrics infra if that's feasible?

miguel: I'll check. If we can't surface raw events we can fallback to storing a separate p999 metric or flagged spike points at ingestion time.

annotations-bot: New annotation created by tara: "outlier-handling-proposal-v1"

tara: Proposed decision (for discussion):
- default: linear axis with visual cap at p99 (explicit cap value in axis label)
- show translucent spike overlay with high-contrast pattern and exact-value tooltip
- legend copy: "Median (P50), P90, P99" and mark capped series with an asterisk + tooltip
- smoothing: default off, header toggle with tooltip explaining algorithm
- accessibility: aria-describedby text explaining capping + overlay; chevron indicator on axis endpoint

zoe: Sounds good. Can someone add a small mock with the chevron and the asterisk in the legend? I can polish the copy after.

sam: I'll sketch it and drop PNG in the thread later today.

tara: Thanks everyone. Filing a short design task for next sprint with these acceptance criteria: axis label includes cap note, overlay renders pattern + tooltip, legend shows asterisk and tooltip, smoothing toggle present.

sam: :rocket:
